battle.name: 黃麞谷之戰
battle.brief: 萬歲通天元年八月，契丹李盡忠在西硤石黃麞谷設伏，誘曹仁師、張玄遇領的二十八將所部輕騎入谷，周軍大敗，張玄遇、龔仁節被俘；李盡忠又用繳獲的軍印偽造軍牒，誘幽州後軍馳援，軍馬疲敝而遭二次截擊，幾乎全滅。卡面希臘重步兵的方陣原理，恰好說明周軍棄步兵、驅輕騎入峽的敗因。

kit.name: 希臘重步兵
kit.history: 方陣的重心不是個人，是互相遮蔽。盾牌接在一起時，一支軍隊的正面比一個人結實。

countries: 黃麞谷之戰是武周與契丹在今河北遷安西硤石谷內的一場決戰，交戰由契丹起兵反周引發。萬歲通天元年正月，契丹松漠都督李盡忠與其妻兄歸誠州刺史孫萬榮舉兵，攻陷營州，殺死營州都督趙文翽；八月，武周進討軍在黃麞谷被契丹伏擊，遭到慘敗。武周一方是唐帝國在武則天治下的中央朝廷與東北邊防體系。調兵遣將由尚書省、兵部與中書門下經手，軍令自洛陽發出，御前則有武將與內廷近臣參預。軍隊以募兵為主，府兵之制在武周時已名存實亡，京畿宿衛與東北邊軍多雜有蕃兵與團練士卒，指揮上的層級是行軍總管、防御使與各道將領。東北的樞紐是營州，治所在今遼寧朝陽，那是契丹、靺鞨諸部交市納貢的市場，歸營州都督管轄；幽州治所在今北京，是關口屏蔽，屯田屯馬所在；清邊道的檀州治所在今北京密雲，橫在契丹南下的要路上。八月之前，周廷已命曹仁師、張玄遇、李多祿、龔仁節等二十八將率師進討，又以武三思為榆關道安撫大使、姚璹為副使出鎮榆關策應。契丹一方則是松漠首領李盡忠與孫萬榮召集的部落聯軍，並非契丹八部的統一軍隊，而是以松漠部為骨幹，加上響應各部與歸附游騎的徵召式聯軍。奪下營州之後，李盡忠自稱可汗、孫萬榮自稱大將，沿用突厥式的名號與編制；李盡忠、孫萬榮所用的松漠都督、歸誠州刺史，正是唐廷授予蕃部首領的羈縻官號，這套用漢式官爵約束邊蕃的做法，最終成了矛盾爆發的地方。叛軍以馬群、皮毛、牲畜為財富核心，戰士多為騎兵，攜弓刀、負標槍，遷徙與作戰合一；營州城內原有的蕃部營帳、馬群與市集貨財被一併奪去，使這支部軍在數日之內便有了遠征的物質基礎。
countriesEn: The battle of Huangshi Valley was a decisive engagement fought inside Xiyashi Valley in what is now Qian'an, Hebei, between the court of Wu Zetian and the Khitan, and it grew out of a Khitan revolt. In the first month of the Wansui Tongtian era, 696, Li Jinzhong, chief of the Khitan Songmo division, and his brother-in-law Sun Wanrong, governor of Guicheng, rose in arms, stormed the city of Yingzhou and killed its military governor Zhao Wenyang; in the eighth month the Zhou field army sent against them was caught in an ambush at Huangshi Valley and destroyed. On the Zhou side stood the central government of the Tang empire under Wu Zetian together with its northeastern frontier system. Troops were mustered and officers appointed through the Department of State Affairs, the Ministry of War and the Secretariat, the orders went out from Luoyang, and at court the decisions were shared by generals and close attendants of the inner palace. The armies were raised chiefly by recruitment, the fubing system having long since become nominal in the time of Wu Zetian, and the capital guards and the northeastern frontier garrisons were mixed with tribal soldiers and locally raised levies; the chain of command ran through the itinerant commandants, the regional defence commissioners and the circuit commanders. The pivot of the northeast was Yingzhou, at modern Chaoyang in Liaoning, the market where the Khitan and the Mohe peoples traded and paid tribute, administered by its own military governor. Youzhou, at modern Beijing, covered the passes and held the agricultural and horse colonies, while Tantzhou, on the Qingbian circuit at modern Miyun in Beijing, lay straight across the road the Khitan would take south. Before August the court had already named Cao Renshi, Zhang Xuanyu, Li Duoluo, Gong Renjie and twenty-six other generals to lead the punitive expedition, and had appointed the Prince of Liang, Wu Sansi, as Pacifying Commissioner of the Yuguan circuit with Yao Tao as his deputy, to hold the passes as a second line of support. The Khitan side was a tribal confederate host raised by Li Jinzhong and Sun Wanrong, not a unified army of the eight Khitan divisions but a levy built on the backbone of the Songmo division, with contingents drawn from the other divisions and from nomads who attached themselves to it. After taking Yingzhou, Li Jinzhong proclaimed himself qaghan and Sun Wanrong a general, adopting the titles and the organisation of the Turks; the offices of Songmo dudu and Guicheng zhou cishi, which Li Jinzhong and Sun Wanrong held, were precisely the Chinese-style titles the Tang court conferred upon tribal chiefs, and this device of governing the frontier through Chinese ranks and titles was where the final contradiction broke open. The rebels counted their wealth in herds of horses, in furs and in livestock; their warriors were for the most part horsemen carrying bows, sabres and javelins, moving and fighting as one. The tribal camps, the stud farms and the market goods of Yingzhou fell with the city, and in a matter of days the rebel host had in its hands the material basis for a campaign deep into Zhou territory.
people: 這場戰爭留下姓名的，多數是武周一方。營州都督趙文翽是起點：他在任上對契丹受災部民不予救濟，謗罵契丹首領、壓制蕃部民眾，怨聲積到不可收拾，最後死在自己治下的營州城裡。契丹一方的主腦是松漠都督李盡忠，他率部先奪營州、自稱可汗，再以老弱詐降、散布契丹難以自保的虛言為餌，把周軍引入谷中；他的妻兄歸誠州刺史孫萬榮任大將，負責帶兵攻城與野戰，七月攻打檀州時被清邊道副總管張九節擊退。周軍主將左鷹揚衛大將軍曹仁師是這一役最關鍵的名字：正是他下令放棄警戒、捨棄步兵而驅輕騎先行，把整支進討軍送進谷口設伏的狹地。右金吾衛大將軍張玄遇與司農少卿龔仁節同在谷中兵敗被俘，兩人都不降，張玄遇寧死不肯為契丹效力，事後更被契丹利用來偽造軍牒。左威衛大將軍李多祿隨軍進討，是二十八將之中名位最重者之一。朝廷事後以梁王武三思為榆關道安撫大使、納言姚璹為副使出鎮榆關策應，試圖在第二道防線上堵住契丹；其後王孝杰再奉命討伐契丹，仍在東硤石谷折戟，兵事一挫再挫。真正在東北站穩腳步的，是其後鎮守幽州的張守珪。契丹方面的其他首領姓名在傳世記載中大多湮沒，李盡忠死後，孫萬榮繼續率眾西進，周朝的東北邊防此後數年都沒有恢復安寧；反倒是唐廷從此認定契丹為患，東北的兵備、外交與用人都換了一套做法。
peopleEn: Most of the names that survive from this war belong to the Zhou side. Zhao Wenyang, the military governor of Yingzhou, is where the story starts: in his administration he refused to relieve the Khitan whose lands had suffered, abused the Khitan chiefs and oppressed the tribal people, and the resentment he piled up finally killed him in the very city he governed. The brain of the Khitan rising was Li Jinzhong, chief of the Songmo division: he took Yingzhou first and proclaimed himself qaghan, and then used the feigned surrender of the old and weak and the rumour that the Khitan could no longer defend themselves as bait to draw the Zhou army into the valley. His brother-in-law Sun Wanrong, governor of Guicheng, served as general, responsible for storming towns and for fighting in the open; in July his attack on Tantzhou was driven back by Zhang Jiejie, deputy commander of the Qingbian circuit. The name that matters most on the Zhou side is Cao Renshi, general of the Left Eagle-Lifting Guard: it was he who ordered the watch relaxed, left the infantry behind and sent the light cavalry forward, delivering the whole punitive army into the narrow ground where the ambush lay. Zhang Xuanyu, general of the Right Gold-Bell Guard, and Gong Renjie, deputy minister of the ministry of agriculture, were defeated in the valley and taken prisoner; neither would submit, Zhang Xuanyu refusing on any terms to serve the Khitan, and the Khitan afterwards turned him to account in the forging of military dispatches. Li Duoluo, general of the Left Martial Guard, marched with the column and was among the highest in rank of the twenty-eight commanders. The court afterwards appointed the Prince of Liang, Wu Sansi, as Pacifying Commissioner of the Yuguan circuit with Yao Tao, formerly a member of the secretariat, as his deputy, to hold the passes and act as a second line; later Wang Xiaojie was sent against the Khitan in turn and was again beaten at East Xiyashi Valley, so that the war went from one reverse to another. The man who actually held the northeast in place was Zhang Shougui, who took charge of Youzhou afterwards. The names of the other Khitan leaders have mostly been lost to the record; after the death of Li Jinzhong, Sun Wanrong carried the host on west, and the Zhou frontier in the northeast was not to recover its peace for years to come. From that time on the court held that the Khitan were a standing danger, and the garrison system, the diplomacy and the men it used in the northeast were all reorganised around that judgement.
kits: 先要說清楚一件容易被誤讀的事：卡面上的希臘重步兵並沒有出現在西硤石谷。那是公元前五世紀地中海世界的產物，青銅科林斯式頭盔、蒙皮與青銅片製成的方形或圓形大盾、護脛、胸甲，加上一支兩公尺左右、可刺可投的長矛與一柄短劍，結成人與人相接的方陣，正面靠盾牌互相遮蔽，縱深靠後排頂住前排。它屬於另一種生態：城邦之間的會戰，平原上列陣，糧道短，供應靠附近的城邑。契丹的草原騎兵與它毫無共同之處。把這件兵器放進黃麞谷之戰，是因為它提供了一條恰好被這場戰役證偽的原理：重步兵的正面強度來自陣形，一旦把步兵撇下、只帶騎兵鑽進峽谷，陣形就不存在，盾牌也就無處可遮。曹仁師在谷口丟開步兵、驅輕騎先行，丟掉的正是這份遮蔽。戰場上的真實裝備，兩邊各有一套。武周進討軍用得最多的是長槊與陌刀：長槊是步戰主力，槊刃細長，配白刃直杆，專為方陣中向前抵禦而造；陌刀身厚重、刃口帶鉸鍔，能在窄地劈砍。遠射靠角弓與弩，弩以蹶張弩、擘張弩為主，張力大但裝填慢，適合守禦固定陣地；步卒多配皮甲或金屬札甲，兜鍪、護臂成套，關內募兵還大量使用紙甲與布甲，輕裝便於在山地峽谷中行軍。騎兵分兩層：重裝騎兵披馬甲、配馬槊，多為將校與骨幹；輕騎即斥候、遊騎與奔騎，不披甲，只攜弓刀，負責追擊與偵察。軍中還有鵲車這類可移動的高台，用來居高觀敵；拒馬與鹿角用來封路；唐初文獻已見以膏油、束草配發火藥製成的火箭，用於焚燒敵方器械與車馬，多屬輔助手段，而非決定戰局的火力。契丹與靺鞨部眾的裝備則完全是騎兵系統：皮毛為甲，或編魚鱗甲、柳葉甲，或穿絮衣式的厚氈；武器以角弓、骨箭、短刀、標槍為主，格鬥另備骨朵一類的狼牙棒，插在馬鞍上供騎手取用。戰馬講究成群不散，傳統上把三匹馬繫成一組，鞍後備披膊甲與箭壺；帳幕用氈，車輛用篷車，財產就是馬群、牛羊與皮毛，隨營有大量牲畜與奶酪，粟米則是口糧的補充。營州城內原有蕃部的市集、馬廄與帳市，被叛軍奪去後，這支部隊才有了持續作戰的本錢。至於攻城器械：營州之失是夜襲與內應得手，並沒有大型攻城器；八月之後的戰事是峽谷與原野的野戰，雙方都沒有雲梯、衝撞車或投石機。真正起作用的地形裝備，是谷口的封鎖與路旁的障礙：契丹把老牛老馬移到路旁，既堵住周軍騎兵的通道，也讓遠道而來的敵人一眼看見契丹已無力自保的假象。
kitsEn: One thing must be said first, because it is easy to misread: the Greek hoplite on the card never set foot in Xiyashi Valley. He was a product of the fifth-century Mediterranean world: a bronze Corinthian helmet, a large square or round shield of wood faced with hide and bronze, greaves and a cuirass, together with a spear about two metres long that could be thrust or thrown and a short sword, all of it arranged into a phalanx in which man covered man, the front protected by overlapping shields and the depth held by the rank behind pressing against the rank in front. He belonged to a different ecology altogether: a set-piece battle between city-states, deployed on open plain, with short supply lines and food drawn from the neighbouring towns. The Khitan cavalry of the steppe shared nothing with him. The weapon is placed in the story of Huangshi Valley because it supplies a principle that this battle happens to refute: the strength of heavy infantry comes from the formation, and the moment the foot is left behind and only mounted men are pushed into a defile, the formation ceases to exist and the shields have nothing to cover. Cao Renshi cast off his infantry at the mouth of the valley and sent the light cavalry in ahead, and what he threw away there was exactly that cover. The real equipment on the field was two systems. The Zhou army used above all the long spear and the modao: the long spear, with a narrow blade and a plain white shaft, was the arm of the battle line, made for pressing forward in formation; the modao was a heavy blade with a hinged guard that could chop in confined ground. Missiles were the composite bow and the crossbow, the latter in its sheeved and braced forms, powerful but slow to reload and therefore suited to holding a fixed position; the foot wore hide or metal lamellar armour with matching helmet and arm guards, and the recruits of the interior were largely issued paper and cloth armour, light enough to march through hill country and gorges. The cavalry came in two layers: armoured riders with caparisoned horses and horse lances, largely officers and the backbone of the host, and light horse, the scouts, outriders and runners, unarmoured, carrying only bow and sabre, for pursuit and reconnaissance. The army also had wheeled observation platforms of the queche type, used to look down on the enemy, and caltrops and antler obstacles for blocking roads; the documents of early Tang already show rockets of burning oil and bound straw fired with a priming charge, used to burn enemy carriages and equipment, an auxiliary means rather than a decisive firepower. The kit of the Khitan and Mohe peoples was purely a mounted system: furs and hide for armour, or rows of fish-scale and willow-leaf plates, or thick felt coats; the weapons were the composite bow, bone arrows, short sabres and javelins, with a club of the wolf-tooth type, the guduo, carried in the saddle for the rider to reach. Warhorses were kept from straying in groups, traditionally three horses tethered together, with a horse blanket and a quiver of arrows behind the saddle; tents were of felt, wagons were covered carts, and wealth was horses, cattle, sheep and furs, with plenty of livestock and dairy on campaign and millet as a supplement to the diet. The market, the stables and the tent-lines of the tribal population inside Yingzhou had to be seized before that host could sustain itself in the field. As for siege engines: Yingzhou fell by night attack and collusion from within, without any great siege machinery, and after August the war was fought in gorges and on open ground, with no ladders, no rams and no stone-throwers on either side. The equipment that really mattered was the blocking of the valley mouth and the obstruction of the road: the Khitan moved old cattle and horses to the roadside, which both plugged the channel the Zhou light cavalry needed and showed the enemy coming in from far away the convincing sight of a people too exhausted to defend themselves.
tactics: 黃麞谷的作戰流程可以拆成七步，每一步都留有文獻痕跡。第一步是奪城造勢。正月十二日李盡忠、孫萬榮舉兵，數日之間攻陷營州、殺趙文翽、掠得蕃部馬群與市貨，奪得軍馬與器械，並立可汗與大將之號；十天之內，兵馬號稱十萬。這既是虛張，也確有其事：營州是東北蕃部交易中心，奪了它就奪了人馬與財貨的來源。第二步是示弱設餌。八月，李盡忠在西硤石谷內預設伏兵，先派被俘的周軍士卒到處散布契丹難以自保的話，又令老弱前來詐降，把老牛老馬趕到路旁擺開，造成一支人馬困頓力竭的模樣。第三步是誘敵深入、鬆懈警覺。周軍信以為真，進軍入谷；曹仁師等將放松戒心，下令捨棄步兵，催督輕騎先行。馬快而陣散，這一步把周軍最需要的遮蔽自己丟掉了。第四步是封谷設伏。黃麞谷在遷安東北的西硤石谷內，道路夾於山崗之間，谷口一封即成絕地。契丹伏兵控兩側坡地與隘口，斷退路、截糧道，等著輕騎進入射程。第五步是谷中交鋒。八月二十八日，周軍前隊入谷即遭襲擊，谷窄馬快，前面的隊形被截斷，後隊看不見前面的旗幟，無法結陣；曹仁師收兵不及，二十八將的指揮序列在谷中瓦解，張玄遇、龔仁節被俘。第六步是假軍牒與二次伏擊。李盡忠用繳獲的周軍印信，令張玄遇在偽造的軍牒上署名，送往幽州方面的後軍，令其放下防區、晝夜兼程趕來。援軍不敢違令，行軍疲敝，軍馬不堪，再度在半途遭契丹截擊，周軍幾乎全滅。一紙假軍令同時毀掉兩支部隊，是這場戰役中最狠的一手。第七步是乘勝擴張。契丹隨後攻陷州縣數十，兵鋒直逼幽州，東北邊防整體崩解。整場戰役最反常的一點是：周軍並非在正面會戰中輸掉的，而是在一次峽谷伏擊與一次偽造命令的伏擊中輸掉的。若周軍把步兵留下結陣、只在谷外以弩弓封住谷口，狹地反而有利於步戰；這正是卡面那套希臘方陣原理的要義，遮蔽來自人與人之間的連接，而不是速度。
tacticsEn: The course of the battle at Huangshi Valley can be broken into seven stages, and each leaves a trace in the record. The first was to seize the city and build a position. On the twelfth day of the first month Li Jinzhong and Sun Wanrong rose in arms; within a few days they had taken Yingzhou, killed Zhao Wenyang, taken the tribal herds and the market goods, seized horses and equipment, and set up the titles of qaghan and general. Within ten days their host was numbered at a hundred thousand. That was in part bluster and in part true: Yingzhou was the market of the northeastern tribes, and taking it meant taking the source of men, horses and wealth. The second stage was to show weakness and lay the bait. In August Li Jinzhong had his ambush prepared inside Xiyashi Valley; he first sent captured Zhou soldiers out to spread the word that the Khitan could no longer defend themselves, and then sent the old and weak forward with a feigned surrender, driving old cattle and horses to the roadside, so that the enemy would see a host worn out and at the end of its strength. The third stage was to draw the enemy deep in and slacken the watch. The Zhou believed it, marched into the valley, and Cao Renshi and the other generals let their guard fall, cast off the infantry and hurried the light cavalry forward. Fast horses and a scattered order: that single step threw away the very cover the Zhou army most needed. The fourth stage was to seal the valley and spring the ambush. Huangshi Valley lies inside Xiyashi Valley northeast of Qian'an, the road hemmed in by hills, and once the mouth is closed it is a killing ground. The Khitan ambushers held the slopes and the defile on both sides, cut the retreat and the supply road, and waited for the light horse to come within range. The fifth stage was the fight in the valley. On the twenty-eighth day of the eighth month the leading files of the Zhou were struck as they entered; the ground was narrow, the horses fast, the front was cut off, and the rear could not see the banners ahead of them and could not form up. Cao Renshi could not recall them, the chain of command of the twenty-eight generals came apart inside the valley, and Zhang Xuanyu and Gong Renjie were taken. The sixth stage was the forged dispatch and the second ambush. Li Jinzhong used the seals of the captured Zhou military offices and had Zhang Xuanyu sign a fabricated dispatch, which was carried to the rear guard in Youzhou with an order to leave their posts and come on at full speed, day and night. The relieving force dared not disobey, marched itself to exhaustion, its horses could go no further, and it was intercepted once more on the road; the Zhou army was very nearly annihilated. A single false order destroyed two armies at once, and that was the cruellest stroke of the whole business. The seventh stage was the exploitation of the victory. The Khitan went on to take dozens of prefectures and counties, drove to the gates of Youzhou, and the whole northeastern frontier collapsed. The most remarkable thing about the campaign is that the Zhou did not lose a set-piece battle: they lost an ambush in a defile and then lost another army to a forged order. Had the Zhou kept their infantry in formation and held the mouth of the valley with bows and crossbows, the narrow ground would have favoured the fight on foot; that is the whole point of the Greek phalanx on the card, that cover comes from the connection between one soldier and the next, and not from speed.
data: 可核對的數字分三類。第一類是文獻自述的日期與名號：萬歲通天元年即696年，正月十二日李盡忠、孫萬榮舉兵反周；正月廿五日，武則天命曹仁師、張玄遇、李多祿、龔仁節等二十八將率軍進討，從起兵到出兵只隔十三日。五月大軍進討；七月十一日再以武三思為榆關道安撫大使、姚璹為副使出鎮榆關策應；七月孫萬榮攻檀州，被張九節擊退；八月二十八日黃麞谷遭伏，張玄遇、龔仁節被俘。奪營州之後，叛軍在十天內兵馬號稱十萬；營州之失，記趙文翽被殺、俘虜數百人。第二類是規模與後果的概括語：黃麞谷一役，周軍幾乎全滅，其後契丹攻陷州縣數十，東北邊防為之一空。這句話出自史家對本役的追述，語氣極重，但仍屬定性而非點名造冊的數字；周軍出動的實際兵額、兩軍的戰死數目，傳世文獻都沒有留下可核的記載，編年只列將名而不記兵數。第三類是可佐證的地理與器物數據：黃麞谷的位置在今河北省遷安市東北的西硤石谷內，營州故城在今遼寧省朝陽市，檀州在今北京市密雲區，榆關即今河北山海關；唐廷在東北的羈縻州有營州、崇州、歸誠州等名。營州故城的考古發掘確認了唐代州城的方形城垣與坊市格局；同一區域出土的唐代窖藏銅錢以開元通寶一類的國朝錢幣為多，契丹與靺鞨諸部在武周時期已廣泛使用中原貨幣交易，這與史書記載的契丹好為市易互相呼應。牛馬、帳幕、粟米這些草原物資的數量，則只有號稱十萬一類的說法，無從核對。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into three classes. The first is what the texts say of dates and names. In the Wansui Tongtian era, that is to say 696, on the twelfth day of the first month Li Jinzhong and Sun Wanrong rose in arms; on the twenty-fifth day of the same month Wu Zetian named Cao Renshi, Zhang Xuanyu, Li Duoluo, Gong Renjie and twenty-six other generals to lead the punitive expedition, only thirteen days between the rising and the marching out. The main force advanced in the fifth month; on the eleventh day of the seventh month Wu Sansi was appointed Pacifying Commissioner of the Yuguan circuit with Yao Tao as his deputy, to hold the passes in support; in the seventh month Sun Wanrong attacked Tantzhou and was driven back by Zhang Jiejie; on the twenty-eighth day of the eighth month the ambush at Huangshi Valley fell on them and Zhang Xuanyu and Gong Renjie were taken. After the taking of Yingzhou the rebels numbered, they claimed, a hundred thousand within ten days; the loss of Yingzhou is recorded with the death of Zhao Wenyang and several hundred prisoners. The second class is the summary language of scale and consequence: at Huangshi Valley the Zhou army was very nearly annihilated, and afterwards the Khitan took dozens of prefectures and counties, so that the northeastern frontier was left without a single usable defence. That sentence is the judgement of the historian upon the campaign, emphatic in tone but a characterisation rather than a roll of names; the actual strength of the Zhou army that marched out, and the casualties of both sides, are nowhere recorded in a form that can be checked, the chronicles listing names of commanders and not numbers of men. The third class is geographical and material data that can be corroborated. Huangshi Valley lies inside Xiyashi Valley northeast of Qian'an in modern Hebei; the site of Yingzhou is at modern Chaoyang in Liaoning; Tantzhou is at modern Miyun in Beijing; Yuguan is the modern Shanhaiguan in Hebei; the Tang administered the northeast through client prefectures that included Yingzhou, Chongzhou and Guicheng. The excavation of the site of Yingzhou has confirmed the square walls and the ward-and-market layout of a Tang prefectural city; hoards of Tang coins found in the same region are largely national issues such as the Kaiyuan Tongbao, and the Khitan and Mohe peoples were already using Chinese coinage for trade in the time of Wu Zetian, which matches what the histories record of their liking for markets. The numbers of cattle, horses, tents and millet are known only through claims such as the hundred thousand, and cannot be checked.
cause: 打起來的原因分四層。最表層是一場治理失誤：營州都督趙文翽對契丹受災部民不予救濟，謗罵契丹首領、壓制蕃部民眾，把本可以用物資安撫的災情變成了怨恨。營州是蕃部與漢地交市納貢的口岸，漢官的傲慢在此最容易變成邊患。第二層是羈縻制度的固有矛盾。唐廷以松漠都督、歸誠州刺史這類漢式官爵授予契丹、靺鞨首領，讓他們替朝廷管住邊地、替朝廷牧馬。這套辦法的前提是朝廷守信用、賞罰有準；一旦營州官的處置與京師的約束脫節，蕃部首領要麼被漢官欺壓而失去部眾的信任，要麼就藉手中的兵馬另立旗幟。叛軍所用的一切，自稱可汗、自稱大將、仿突厥名號，都是先用唐的官爵取得部眾，再用草原的稱號自立。第三層是草原部落的內部整合壓力。契丹八部此時尚未統一，松漠部趁亂壯大，孫萬榮又以妻兄與大將的身分站在李盡忠一邊，聯盟內的權力分配本身就靠奪城、奪馬、奪牲畜來衡量；營州一失，誰掌握蕃部的人馬與物資，誰就是新的契丹之主。第四層是周廷的反應機制失靈。契丹在正月初舉兵，到正月二十五日武則天才下詔命將，前後十三日，這十三日裡營州已失、趙文翽已死。兵部與諸道對蕃部的情報本該在事前就有，只是訊息傳不到，或者傳到了而無人敢斷言，於是周廷用了一次倉促的、靠二十八將拼湊的出擊，而沒有先封住營州、再斷其退路這類更穩妥的辦法。值得注意的是，東北方同時正有另一支力量在迅速上升，粟末靺鞨的首領大祚榮稍後建國，東北的兩蕃格局就在這幾年裡成形。契丹的反亂因此不只是一場邊地叛亂，而是改變了整個東北政治版圖的開場。
causeEn: The reasons for the war lie in four layers. At the surface lies a failure of administration: the military governor of Yingzhou, Zhao Wenyang, refused to relieve the Khitan whose lands had suffered, abused the Khitan chiefs and oppressed the tribal people, turning a disaster that might have been answered with grain and cloth into a reservoir of grudge. Yingzhou was the port where the tribes traded and paid tribute to the Chinese world, and there the arrogance of Han officials turned into frontier war most easily. The second layer is the contradiction built into the client system. The Tang court conferred Chinese-style titles such as Songmo dudu and Guicheng zhou cishi upon Khitan and Mohe chiefs, making them responsible for holding the frontier and for herding horses on the court's behalf. The arrangement presupposed that the court kept its word and that rewards and punishments were consistent; once the conduct of the official at Yingzhou drifted away from the court's restraint, a tribal chief was either ground down by the Chinese official and lost the trust of his people, or he used the troops and horses under his hand to raise a banner of his own. Everything the rebels used, the self-styled qaghan, the self-styled general, the titles copied from the Turks, follows the same pattern: first the Chinese titles to win the people over, then the steppe titles to stand on their own. The third layer is the pressure of internal consolidation among the steppe divisions. The eight Khitan divisions were not yet united, the Songmo division grew strong on the strength of the revolt, and Sun Wanrong stood beside Li Jinzhong as brother-in-law and general; within such a confederation power was measured by cities taken, horses taken and livestock taken. Once Yingzhou fell, whoever held the tribesmen, the horses and the goods of the tribes was the new master of the Khitan. The fourth layer is the failure of the court's response. The Khitan rose in the first month, and Wu Zetian did not issue the order appointing generals until the twenty-fifth day of that month, thirteen days later, and in those thirteen days Yingzhou had already fallen and Zhao Wenyang was already dead. The Ministry of War and the circuits should have had intelligence on the tribes in advance; the news either did not travel or travelled and could not be acted upon. So the court launched a hasty expedition patched together out of twenty-eight commanders instead of taking the sounder course of sealing Yingzhou first and then cutting the rebels off from their retreat. It is worth noting that another power was rising fast in the northeast at the same time, the leader of the Sumi Mohe, Da Zuorong, who would found a state a few years later; the pattern of the two tribes in the northeast took shape in these very years. The Khitan rising was therefore not merely a frontier rebellion but the opening of a complete reordering of the political map of the northeast.
impact: 黃麞谷之後，東北方局勢急轉直下，影響的深度遠超一場邊戰。第一，營州、崇州、檀州相繼失守，契丹攻陷州縣數十，兵鋒直抵幽州城下，東北邊防體系整體崩解；此後數年，周廷對遼東的實際控制只剩下幽州一線的幾個據點，張守珪鎮幽州、築城浚壕、練兵屯田，才勉強把局勢穩住。第二，契丹從邊部落族變成東北的主人。李盡忠死後，孫萬榮繼續西進，一度打到柳城、威脅河北，把契丹可患的判斷深深刻進唐廷的東北政策裡。此後唐對契丹改採以封賞、互市、羈縻和暫時容忍為主的辦法，兵力重心轉向吐蕃與西域，東北則以邊將的個人能力和地形屏障代替中央的常設控制。安史之亂時，契丹兵被安祿山借用來攻河北；亂平之後，契丹又趁勢入寇幽州，逼迫唐廷議和。從這個角度說，黃麞谷是唐廷在東北失去主動權的起點。第三，軍事技術與邊防觀念被迫更新。營州、崇州這些蕃漢雜處的州城失守，暴露了城防依賴蕃部附庸、而附庸一旦反噬就無險可守的弱點；黃麞谷的教訓則更直接，峽谷地形的守方只要控制谷口、封死退路，就足以吃掉遠來的大軍。中原兵家後來講避實擊虛、講用間、講示弱誘敵，講的正是這場戰役裡契丹用過的辦法。第四，與契丹同期，靺鞨在北方另起渤海國，東北出現了兩個互相牽制的蕃部政權，唐初設置的安東都護府框架實際上名存實亡。第五，戰役本身留下的記載極少，戰場至今沒有確認的遺址；它的細節主要靠史書中一段記述與後人轉述保存下來，許多數字與人名至今仍有異說，讀史時須存疑。
impactEn: After Huangshi Valley the situation in the northeast turned swiftly, and the consequences reached far beyond a border skirmish. First, Yingzhou, Chongzhou and Tantzhou fell in turn, the Khitan took dozens of prefectures and counties and drove to the walls of Youzhou, and the whole northeastern frontier system came apart; for years afterwards the effective reach of the Zhou court over Liaodong was reduced to a few strong points on the Youzhou line, and only Zhang Shougui, holding Youzhou, building walls, digging ditches, drilling troops and opening land, brought the position back into some order. Second, the Khitan changed from a tribe on the border into the master of the northeast. After the death of Li Jinzhong, Sun Wanrong carried the host on west as far as Liucheng and into the shadow of Hebei, and the judgement that the Khitan were a standing danger was driven deep into the policy of the court. From then on the Tang treated the Khitan mainly by investiture, mutual markets, client titles and a policy of temporary acquiescence; the weight of the army went to Tibet and the western regions, and in the northeast the standing control of the centre was replaced by the personal ability of the frontier commanders and by the country's own barriers of terrain. When the An Lushan rebellion broke out, Khitan troops were borrowed by An Lushan to strike into Hebei; after the revolt was put down the Khitan invaded Youzhou again and forced the court into negotiations. From this angle Huangshi Valley is the starting point of the loss of initiative in the northeast. Third, military technique and the idea of frontier defence had to be revised. The loss of towns such as Yingzhou and Chongzhou, where Chinese and tribal populations lived together, exposed the weakness of a city defence that rested on tribal clients who, once they turned, left the city with nothing to hold it. The lesson of Huangshi Valley is even plainer: in a defile, the side that holds the mouth and closes the retreat can destroy a large army that has marched a long way. When the writers of the central plain afterwards spoke of avoiding the strong and striking the weak, of using spies, of showing weakness to draw the enemy in, they were describing what the Khitan had actually done in this campaign. Fourth, at the same time as the Khitan, the Mohe raised the state of Bohai in the north, and two rival tribal powers faced each other in the northeast, while the framework of the Andong Protectorate set up at the beginning of the Tang had become nominal in all but name. Fifth, very little was left on the ground, and the battlefield has never been securely identified; the details of the campaign survive through a single passage in the histories and through later retellings, and many of the figures and names remain disputed, so that they have to be read with caution.
result: 八月二十八日，黃麞谷的結局落定。周軍前隊入谷即被截斷，前面的隊形散在狹窄的谷道裡，後隊看不見旗幟，曹仁師收兵不及；張玄遇、龔仁節被俘，兩人都不肯降。曹仁師等將放棄步兵、只催輕騎先行這一步，決定了全軍的命運。戰後李盡忠用繳獲的周軍印信偽造軍牒，令張玄遇署名，送往幽州，誘使後軍總管與宗懷昌等部放棄防區、晝夜兼程馳援；援軍疲於奔命，軍馬不堪，再遭半途截擊，周軍幾乎全滅。前一役靠山谷，後一役靠一道假命令，八月之內兩支大軍相繼覆沒，東北邊防從此無險可守。契丹乘勝追擊，攻陷州縣數十，一度兵臨幽州；武則天再命王孝杰討之，仍在東硤石谷折戟，直到後來幽州換將、且朝廷改取招撫分化，契丹的勢頭才被壓下去。就結果而言，黃麞谷之戰是契丹反亂的決定性一仗，也是武周在東北的一次徹底失敗。它沒有改變中原的政局，卻徹底改變了東北的權力格局：唐廷失去營州、崇州等關鍵州城，契丹則以松漠部為核心完成了一次成功的擴張，草原與農耕的邊界往南推了一大截。史家常把這場戰役與隋朝征高句麗的失敗並提，說的都是同一個道理：大軍深入、糧道拉長、指揮鬆散，又被對手引入地利，最終再大的兵力也保不住勝果。而卡面那件希臘重步兵，在這場戰役裡其實是一面反面鏡。方陣的道理誰都懂，靠盾牌互相遮蔽、靠縱深頂住前排，才是重步兵的長處；可惜曹仁師在谷口把步兵丟了，把整支軍隊的正面交給了速度，等於把遮蔽全部作廢。一千二百年前的希臘人靠方陣贏，同一場峽谷裡的唐軍靠方陣輸，差別從來不在盾牌，而在有沒有人把它帶進戰場。
resultEn: On the twenty-eighth day of the eighth month the outcome of Huangshi Valley was settled. The leading files of the Zhou were cut off the moment they entered; the front was scattered in the narrow track of the valley, the rear could not see the banners ahead, and Cao Renshi could not call them back. Zhang Xuanyu and Gong Renjie were taken, and neither would submit. The single order of Cao Renshi and the other generals to cast off the infantry and hurry the light cavalry forward decided the fate of the whole army. Afterwards Li Jinzhong used the seals of the captured Zhou military offices, had Zhang Xuanyu sign a fabricated dispatch and sent it to Youzhou, tempting the rear command and the men of Zong Huichang to leave their posts and come on at full speed, day and night. The relieving force was worn out by its march, its horses could go no further, it was intercepted once more on the road, and the Zhou army was very nearly annihilated. One ambush in a valley and then one more ambush on a forged order destroyed two armies within a single month, and the northeast frontier was left with nothing to stand on. The Khitan pressed on, took dozens of prefectures and counties and came in sight of Youzhou; Wu Zetian sent Wang Xiaojie against them in turn, and he was beaten again at East Xiyashi Valley, and it was only later, with a change of commanders at Youzhou and a shift in court policy towards pacification and division, that the Khitan were pushed back. As a result, the battle of Huangshi Valley was the decisive stroke of the Khitan rising and a thorough defeat for the Zhou in the northeast. It changed nothing in the politics of the central plain, but it changed the balance of power in the northeast completely: the court lost the key prefectures of Yingzhou and Chongzhou, while the Khitan, centred on the Songmo division, completed a successful expansion, pushing the frontier between steppe and farmland a long way south. Historians often set this campaign beside the failures of the Sui wars against Goguryeo, and the point is the same in both cases: a great army marching deep, its supply line stretched, its command loose, led by the enemy into ground of the enemy's choosing, and then no amount of numbers saves the result. The Greek hoplite on the card, in all this, serves as a mirror held up to the wrong. Everyone understood the phalanx: cover comes from overlapping shields, depth comes from the rank behind pressing forward, and that is the strength of heavy infantry. Cao Renshi left his infantry at the mouth of the valley and gave the face of the whole army over to speed, which threw the cover away entirely. The Greeks of twelve hundred years before won with the phalanx; the Tang army of the same defile lost with it. The difference was never in the shield, but in whether anybody brought it into the field.
